1: The nucleon number is the total of protons and neutrons, and the proton number fixes the element. Isotopes share a proton number but differ in neutron number, so their nucleon numbers differ.
2: Most alpha particles pass straight through, but a few are deflected strongly. This could only happen if almost all the mass and positive charge are concentrated in a very small nucleus.
3: Thermionic emission works because the thermal energy of the electrons overcomes the work function of the metal. An electric field then accelerates the released electrons.
4: A linear accelerator uses alternating fields along a line, with each stage timed so the particles are accelerated at every gap. This keeps the particles in step with the field.
5: A magnetic field provides the centripetal force, so QvB = mv²/r, which rearranges to r = p/(BQ). A larger momentum gives a larger radius, which is how mass and momentum can be measured.
